Ceuta and Melilla: Spain-Morocco dispute over enclaves continues

The Spanish enclaves of Ceuta and Melilla, located on the North African coast, remain a point of contention between Spain and Morocco. Morocco has claimed sovereignty over these territories since the 1960s. This dispute was reignited by the arrival of over 72,000 migrants in Ceuta from Morocco during the summer. King Felipe VI's planned visit to Ceuta on October 13 was intended as a symbolic gesture following this migration crisis, which strained the enclave's social cohesion.
